Use when the user mentions ChordPro or .cho/.crd/.pro files, `[C]lyric` inline chords or `{title:}`/`{start_of_chorus}` directives, the `chordpro`/`a2crd` CLI, converting chords-over-lyrics (Ultimate Guitar/OnSong) text, fetching lyrics (LRCLIB/Mojim/Musixmatch), or extracting chords from a YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud link or mp3/wav. References chordpro.org.
4	---
5	
6	# chordpro
7	
8	Produce and work with [ChordPro](https://www.chordpro.org/) chord sheets — the
9	plain-text format where chords live inline in the lyrics as `[C]like [G]this`.
10	This skill is a **router that degrades gracefully**: it picks the most reliable
11	workflow for whatever the user actually has (a `.cho` file, a chords-over-lyrics
12	paste, bare lyrics, an audio file, or just a song title) and every path ends by
13	**validating** the output. It is honest about the one hard part — extracting
14	chords from raw audio is an ~80%-accurate *draft*, never an oracle — and falls
15	back to interactive, fill-in-the-gaps assistance instead of pretending otherwise.
16	
17	## When to use
18	
19	- User names **ChordPro** / `.cho` / `.crd` / `.chopro` / `.pro`, inline
20	  `[C]lyric` chords, or `{title:}` / `{start_of_chorus}` / `{soc}` directives.
21	- Convert an existing sheet: **chords-over-lyrics** text (Ultimate Guitar, OnSong,
22	  a lyric with chord letters on the line above) → ChordPro.
23	- Render / transpose / validate a `.cho` with the **`chordpro`** or **`a2crd`** CLI.
24	- "Make a chord sheet for <song>" starting from **lyrics only**, or from a
25	  **YouTube / Bilibili / SoundCloud link** or an **mp3 / wav** file.
26	- Ask about **lyrics sources** (Mojim/魔鏡, KKBOX, Musixmatch, LRCLIB, Genius,
27	  NetEase, QQ Music) — which give time-synced `.lrc` vs plain text.
28	
29	## When NOT to use
30	
31	- **Engraving staff notation** (notes on a staff, MusicXML / MIDI / LilyPond /
32	  MuseScore output) — ChordPro is lyrics+chords, not a score. Hand off to a
33	  notation tool. (ChordPro *can* embed ABC/LilyPond fragments — see the format
34	  reference — but it is not an engraver.)
35	- **OMR from a scanned score image** (photo/PDF of printed sheet music → notes)
36	  is out of scope; there is no reliable open path. Offer manual transcription
37	  into ChordPro instead, and say so plainly.
38	
39	## Authoritative sources
40	
41	- Format + directives + CLI: **https://www.chordpro.org/** (link, don't
42	  paraphrase from memory — the directive set evolves).
43	- Source / releases: **https://github.com/ChordPro/chordpro**.
44	
45	## The router — pick the workflow by what the user has
46	
47	| User has… | Do this | Reliability |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| A `.cho`/`.crd`/`.pro` file | Render / transpose / **validate** via `chordpro` CLI | High |
50	| **Chords-over-lyrics** text (UG/OnSong) | `a2crd` → light manual cleanup → validate | High |
51	| **Lyrics only** | Fetch/confirm lyrics → **interactively** fill chords (propose from key, ask the user to confirm/correct) | Medium (human-in-loop) |
52	| An **audio file or link** | `scripts/audio-to-chords.py` → *draft* with `AUTO-GENERATED` header → human correction | ~80% draft |
53	| Only a **song title** | Fetch lyrics (LRCLIB) ± audio → then one of the above | Depends |
54	
55	Always prefer the highest row that fits. Don't jump to the audio pipeline when
56	the user already pasted chords — `a2crd` will be faster and correct.
57	
58	## ChordPro cheat-sheet + output template
59	
60	- **Extensions**: `.cho` (recommended), also `.crd` `.chopro` `.chord` `.pro`.
61	  Plain UTF-8. `#` starts a comment line; blank lines separate blocks.
62	- **Inline chords**: `[C]` immediately before the syllable it sits over —
63	  `Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot`. Annotations (non-chords): `[*softly]`.
64	- **Metadata**: `{title:}`/`{t:}`, `{subtitle:}`/`{st:}`, `{artist:}`,
65	  `{composer:}`, `{album:}`, `{year:}`, `{key:}`, `{tempo:}`, `{time:}`, `{capo:}`.
66	- **Environments** (long / short): chorus `{start_of_chorus}`/`{soc}` …
67	  `{end_of_chorus}`/`{eoc}`; verse `{sov}`…`{eov}`; bridge `{sob}`…`{eob}`;
68	  tab (monospaced, chords NOT parsed) `{sot}`…`{eot}`. Recall a chorus with
69	  `{chorus}`. Comments: `{comment:}`/`{c:}`.
70	
71	Emit this shape — metadata block → environments/comments → verses/choruses:
72	
73	```
74	{title: Swing Low Sweet Chariot}
75	{artist: Traditional}
76	{key: G}
77	{tempo: 90}
78	{time: 4/4}
79	
80	{comment: Intro}
81	[G] [C] [G] [D]
82	
83	{start_of_chorus: Chorus}
84	Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot,
85	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
86	{end_of_chorus}
87	
88	{start_of_verse: Verse 1}
89	I [G]looked over Jordan, and [C]what did I [G]see,
90	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
91	{end_of_verse}
92	
93	{chorus}
94	```
95	
96	Full directive set (chord `{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup, ABC/LilyPond
97	blocks, `x_` custom namespace) → read `references/chordpro-format.md`.
98	
99	## The `chordpro` / `a2crd` CLI (essentials)
100	
101	The official tool is a Perl program (CPAN dist **`App::Music::ChordPro`**). Current
102	6.x releases install the **`chordpro`** command; the chords-over-lyrics importer
103	is `chordpro --a2crd` (a standalone `a2crd` binary shipped in older releases and
104	may be absent — prefer `chordpro --a2crd`).
105	
106	```bash
107	# Install (macOS — there is NO official Homebrew formula; use CPAN)
108	brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro
109	# If `chordpro` then errors "Can't locate ChordPro.pm", activate local::lib once:
110	eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"   # add to ~/.zshrc to persist
111	
112	# Render
113	chordpro -o song.pdf song.cho          # PDF (format inferred from extension)
114	chordpro --generate=HTML -o song.html song.cho
115	
116	# Transpose (N semitones; suffix s/f forces sharp/flat spelling)
117	chordpro -x 2  -o up.pdf   song.cho
118	chordpro -x -3f -o down.pdf song.cho
119	
120	# Convert chords-over-lyrics text -> ChordPro (the official importer)
121	chordpro --a2crd input.txt -o song.cho
122	```
123	
124	Install-per-platform, generators, config JSON, songbook `--toc`, and `a2crd`
125	heuristic tuning → read `references/cli-and-rendering.md`.
126	
127	## Verify loop — never hand back an unvalidated `.cho`
128	
129	Every generated or edited file goes through the parser before you present it:
130	
131	```bash
132	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # wraps the command below; PASS/FAIL + warnings
133	# equivalently:
134	chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o - song.cho   # exit 0 + no stderr warnings = valid
135	```
136	
137	To auto-normalize to canonical form (fix spacing, round-trip directives):
138	`chordpro --generate=ChordPro -o song.cho song.cho`. If `chordpro` isn't
139	installed, the script prints the install one-liner — say so and offer to proceed
140	without rendering (the format is still human-checkable).
141	
142	## Generating from audio / links — honest limits
143	
144	This is the ambitious path and the shakiest. **Set expectations first**: open
145	automatic chord recognition tops out around **78–80% on simple major/minor pop**
146	and drops sharply on 7ths, extended/jazz chords, key changes, and quiet or dense
147	mixes; inversions/slash chords are unreliable; and it cannot know the capo a
148	guitarist used. Treat the result as a **draft to correct**, not a transcription.
149	
150	```bash
151	# Best-effort turnkey: link or local file -> draft ChordPro
152	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py --dry-run "https://youtu.be/..."   # show the plan first
153	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py -o draft.cho "https://youtu.be/..."
154	```
155	
156	The script downloads audio with `yt-dlp` (YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud) and runs
157	`chord-extractor`/Chordino. Its output **must** carry the
158	`{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}` header. On macOS the
159	Chordino Vamp plugin often isn't installed; the script detects that and prints
160	exact install guidance + manual alternatives instead of crashing — relay that to
161	the user rather than silently failing. Tool comparison, beat/key detection, and
162	commercial escape hatches (Moises/Songsterr have APIs; Chordify/Chord AI/Ultimate
163	Guitar don't) → read `references/audio-to-chords.md`.
164	
165	**Legal**: only process content the user owns or has the right to use, for
166	personal use, locally; downloading copyrighted audio can violate a platform's
167	ToS. Surface this — don't bury it.
168	
169	## Lyrics sources
170	
171	Default to **LRCLIB** — free, no API key, returns time-synced `.lrc`:
172	
173	```bash
174	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
175	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..."   # plain text
176	```
177	
178	| Source | Access | Synced `.lrc`? |
179	|---|---|---|
180	| **LRCLIB** | free, no key | **yes** |
181	| Musixmatch | API key; full/synced is paid | yes (paid) |
182	| NetEase / QQ Music | unofficial community APIs | yes (Chinese catalog) |
183	| Genius (`lyricsgenius`) | API token; lyrics scraped from page | no (plain) |
184	| Mojim / 魔鏡 | scrape-only | no (plain) |
185	| KKBOX | partner-gated | n/a |
186	
187	Full comparison, legality, and the LRCLIB API → read `references/lyrics-sources.md`.
188	
189	## Available scripts
190	
191	- **`scripts/validate-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — verify a file parses cleanly
192	  (`chordpro --strict`); PASS/FAIL to stdout, warnings to stderr. Guides install
193	  if `chordpro` is missing. Flags: `--help`.
194	- **`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py`** — fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced `.lrc` default,
195	  `--plain` for text). Self-contained via `uv run`. Flags: `--artist`, `--track`,
196	  `--duration`, `--album`, `--plain`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
197	- **`scripts/audio-to-chords.py`** — best-effort link/audio → draft ChordPro
198	  (`yt-dlp` + `chord-extractor`). Degrades gracefully when the ACR backend is
199	  unavailable. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--lrc`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
200	
201	## Bundled assets
202	
203	Ready-to-open examples + a template under `assets/` (all songs are **public
204	domain**; every `.cho` validates clean with `chordpro --strict`). Use them as
205	copy-paste starting points and few-shot references:
206	
207	- `assets/example-amazing-grace.cho` — simplest real song: metadata + inline chords.
208	- `assets/example-when-the-saints.cho` — chorus/verse structure + `{chorus}` recall.
209	- `assets/example-greensleeves.cho` — feature showcase: `{define}` diagrams, a

211	- `assets/template-song.cho` — fill-in-the-blanks scaffold (renders as-is); the

213	- `assets/example-synced-lyrics.lrc` — sample time-synced `.lrc` (what

217	
218	## Reference files
219	
220	- `references/chordpro-format.md` — Read **when** hand-authoring or you need a
221	  directive beyond the cheat-sheet (`{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup,
222	  ABC/LilyPond, `x_` custom namespace).
223	- `references/cli-and-rendering.md` — Read **when** installing, rendering,
224	  transposing, converting with `a2crd`, or validating/normalizing.
225	- `references/audio-to-chords.md` — Read **when** the user wants chords from an
226	  audio file or a link (ACR tool choice, beat/key, limits, escape hatches).
227	- `references/lyrics-sources.md` — Read **when** fetching lyrics (source table,
228	  synced-vs-plain, API-vs-scrape, legality, LRCLIB API).
229	
230	## Gotchas
231	
232	- **macOS has no official Homebrew `chordpro`** — install via CPAN
233	  (`brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`). A signed `.dmg`
234	  GUI exists on GitHub Releases but the CLI is the CPAN route.
235	- **`Can't locate ChordPro.pm in @INC` after cpanm** — cpanm installed into a
236	  `local::lib` (`~/perl5`) that isn't on Perl's path. Activate it:
237	  `eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"` (persist in `~/.zshrc`).
238	- **No standalone `a2crd` in ChordPro 6.x** — use `chordpro --a2crd input.txt`.
239	  Its output needs a human pass (heuristic, column-based chord placement); always
240	  validate and eyeball before rendering.
241	- **Angle brackets `< >` are text markup in ChordPro v6.** Don't put `<...>`
242	  placeholders in lyrics/chords — the parser reads `<b>`/`<i>`-style markup and
243	  floods warnings. Use plain-text placeholders (see `assets/template-song.cho`).
244	- **No official online validator.** chordpro.org hosts docs + a desktop GUI, not
245	  a "try it online" box. Validate locally with the CLI (`validate-cho.sh`).
246	- **Chord accuracy from audio is ~80% at best** on simple pop, worse otherwise.
247	  Never present a machine-extracted sheet without the `AUTO-GENERATED` header and
248	  a "verify chords/key/timing" caveat.
249	- **Detected key is a suggestion.** ACR outputs absolute pitches; key detection
250	  confuses relative major/minor and keys a fifth apart, and enharmonic spelling
251	  (Gb vs F#) is ambiguous. Confirm with the user before committing `{key:}`.
252	- **Chords in `{sot}`…`{eot}` tab blocks are NOT parsed** — that's for ASCII tab.
253	  Use inline `[..]` in verses/choruses; reserve tab blocks for fret diagrams.
254	- **Lyrics/audio ToS.** Prefer LRCLIB (open); most other lyric sources are
255	  scrape-only or paid, and downloading audio has copyright/ToS limits. Keep it
256	  personal-use and local; surface the caveat rather than hiding it.

```text
1	# Audio / link → chords: feasibility, tools, and honest limits
2	
3	Read this when the user wants chords from an audio file or a
4	YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud link. **The headline: this is a draft generator,
5	not a transcriber.** Set that expectation before running anything.
6	
7	## Accuracy reality — say this out loud
8	
9	Open automatic chord recognition (ACR) at the current state of the art (MIREX
10	2024/2025 Audio Chord Estimation) tops out around **78–80% WCSR on major/minor**,
11	dropping to the **mid-60s% for sevenths**. Models "excel on frequent major/minor
12	chords but underperform on rare seventh and extended chords." So even on simple
13	pop, roughly **1 second in 5 is mislabeled**; jazz, modulations, quiet intros,
14	and dense mixes are much worse, and **inversions / slash chords are unreliable**.
15	The tool also outputs *absolute* pitches — it cannot know the capo a guitarist
16	used. Every machine-extracted sheet ships with a
17	`{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}` header.
18	
19	## The pipeline
20	
21	```
22	link ─▶ yt-dlp (→ wav)
23	        └▶ [optional] Demucs stem separation (isolate harmonic content — can help ACR)
24	        ─▶ ACR (chord-extractor/Chordino | madmom CNN | Omnizart) ─▶ chord timeline (.lab)
25	        ─▶ beats/downbeats (madmom) + key (Essentia/librosa) ─▶ bar grid + key/tempo
26	lyrics ─▶ LRCLIB (synced) ─first── else ─▶ Musixmatch ─ else ─▶ scrape/plain
27	        └▶ if PLAIN only: forced alignment (WhisperX) to recover line timing
28	merge  ─▶ snap chord onsets to beats; place [Chord] at nearest change per lyric line
29	output ─▶ ChordPro draft with AUTO-GENERATED header + {key}/{tempo}
30	```
31	
32	`scripts/audio-to-chords.py` automates the download → ACR → skeleton portion and
33	degrades gracefully when the ACR backend is missing.
34	
35	## Getting audio: `yt-dlp`
36	
37	Supports **YouTube, SoundCloud, AND Bilibili** (1000+ sites). Needs **ffmpeg**
38	for `-x` audio extraction.
39	
40	```bash
41	# best audio -> wav (best for analysis); swap wav->mp3 for MP3
42	yt-dlp -x --audio-format wav --audio-quality 0 -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" "URL"
43	```
44	
45	- **Bilibili**: public videos work; higher-res/member content needs
46	  `--cookies-from-browser chrome`.
47	- **SoundCloud**: public tracks work; some are download-disabled/private.
48	- **Legal/ToS**: downloading copyrighted audio generally violates the platform's
49	  ToS and can infringe copyright. Frame as **personal-use, user-owns-or-has-rights**,
50	  process **locally**, **don't redistribute**. Surface this to the user.
51	
52	## ACR tools (audio → time-stamped chords)
53	
54	| Tool | Status (2026) | Invoke | Vocab | When to pick |
55	|---|---|---|---|---|
56	| **chord-extractor** (ohollo) | Maintained (v0.1.3, Aug 2025); wraps **Chordino** | `pip install chord-extractor`; `Chordino(roll_on=1).extract('song.wav')` | maj/min + some 7ths | **Default.** Turnkey on Linux; on macOS/Windows needs a Vamp plugin pack + `VAMP_PATH` (the friction point) |
57	| **madmom** CNN | NN models are best-in-class but install is painful (classifiers cap at Py 3.7; use 3.8–3.9 or the `imcmurray/madmom-modern` fork) | `CNNChordFeatureProcessor` + `CRFChordRecognitionProcessor` | maj/min | Higher accuracy when you can pin the env; also gives **beats/downbeats** |
58	| **Omnizart** | Actively maintained; Docker; Py ≥3.8; heavy (TF + fluidsynth) | `omnizart download-checkpoints` → `omnizart chord transcribe in.wav` | richer | Heavyweight multitask toolbox (also drums/melody/vocal) |
59	| **Chordino / NNLS-Chroma** (Vamp) | Mature C++; the engine under the above | `sonic-annotator -d vamp:nnls-chroma:chordino:simplechord in.wav -w csv` | maj/min + basic 7ths | Cross-platform CLI baseline without Python glue |
60	| **autochord** | Effectively frozen (last release 2021; TF-1.x rot) | `pip install autochord`; `autochord.recognize('a.wav','chords.lab')` | **25: 12 maj + 12 min + N only** | Only if others fail; major/minor only |
61	| **Hugging Face** | Research/demo-grade; **no stable plug-and-play audio→chord model** | Spaces like `tigorsinaga/AI_CHORD_RECOGNITION`; repos `chord-engine`, `Audio-Chord-Recognition` | varies | Mention as "cutting edge", don't depend on it. (`musiclang` is *symbolic* generation, not audio→chord) |
62	
63	**macOS note**: `chord-extractor`'s bundled Chordino binary is Linux-only. On
64	macOS you must install the NNLS-Chroma Vamp plugin and set `VAMP_PATH`, OR fall
65	back to `sonic-annotator` with the plugin, OR run in a Linux container. The
66	script detects the missing plugin and prints this guidance.
67	
68	## Beat / downbeat + key (complements chords)
69	
70	- **madmom** — best NN **beat/downbeat** (`RNNDownBeatProcessor` +
71	  `DBNDownBeatTrackingProcessor`); downbeats give the bar grid to snap chords to.
72	- **librosa** — pure-Python, trivial install: `librosa.beat.beat_track` (tempo +
73	  beats); chroma for a hand-rolled Krumhansl-Schmuckler key estimate.
74	- **Essentia** — `KeyExtractor` (key+scale), `RhythmExtractor2013`; heavier install.
75	- **KeyFinder** — desktop GUI, not a library (`libKeyFinder` C++ if binding).
76	
77	**Key caveat**: detection is ~70–90% and confuses relative major/minor and
78	keys a fifth apart. Treat detected key as a *suggestion*; confirm with the user.
79	
80	## Where it breaks (tell the user)
81	
82	1. Chord accuracy (~80% simple pop; worse on 7ths/jazz/modulation/quiet/dense).
83	2. Chord↔lyric alignment — chords are timestamped; mapping to the exact *syllable*
84	   needs word-level lyric timing (rare — Musixmatch richsync / QQ KRC). Most
85	   drafts land chords at **line** granularity; a human nudges them.
86	3. Capo/key ambiguity + enharmonic spelling.
87	4. Vocabulary mismatch (maj/min-only tools oversimplify sus/add/7 songs).
88	5. Lyrics coverage gaps for niche/Chinese/live tracks → scrape or ASR fallback.
89	
90	## Commercial / reference escape hatches (name-drop only)
91	
92	- **Moises** — real developer/extensions platform (`extensions.moises.ai`,
93	  request access): stems, chords, beat. The one with genuine API access.
94	- **Songsterr** — public API for tabs/chords (CORS-restricted → server-side).
95	- **Chordify** — no official public API.
96	- **Chord AI** — explicitly no API.
97	- **Ultimate Guitar** — no official public API (third-party scrapers only).
98	
99	## Selected sources
100	
101	- chord-extractor: https://github.com/ohollo/chord-extractor
102	- madmom chords: https://madmom.readthedocs.io/en/v0.16/modules/features/chords.html ·
103	  modern fork https://github.com/imcmurray/madmom-modern
104	- Omnizart: https://github.com/Music-and-Culture-Technology-Lab/omnizart
105	- NNLS-Chroma / Chordino: https://isophonics.net/nnls-chroma.html
106	- MIREX ACE results: https://www.music-ir.org/mirex/wiki/2025:Audio_Chord_Estimation_Results
107	- yt-dlp: https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp
108	- Moises API: https://extensions.moises.ai/api-reference · Songsterr API:
109	  https://www.songsterr.com/a/wsa/api-tabs-a26570
110
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
4	# dependencies = [
5	#   "yt-dlp>=2024.1",
6	# ]
7	# ///
8	"""audio-to-chords.py — best-effort link/audio -> DRAFT ChordPro.
9	
10	This is a draft generator, NOT a transcriber. Open automatic chord recognition
11	tops out around ~80% on simple major/minor pop and is worse on 7ths, jazz, key
12	changes, and dense mixes; the detected key is a suggestion, and inversions/slash
13	chords are unreliable. Output always carries an AUTO-GENERATED header — a human
14	must verify chords, key, and timing. See references/audio-to-chords.md.
15	
16	Pipeline: URL --(yt-dlp)--> wav --(chord-extractor/Chordino)--> chord timeline
17	--> ChordPro skeleton. If an .lrc is supplied (--lrc), chords are placed at line
18	granularity onto the lyric lines.
19	
20	    uv run audio-to-chords.py --dry-run "https://youtu.be/..."
21	    uv run audio-to-chords.py -o draft.cho "https://youtu.be/..."
22	    uv run audio-to-chords.py --lrc song.lrc --title "Hello" song.wav -o draft.cho
23	
24	LEGAL: only process content you own or have the right to use, for personal use,
25	locally. Downloading copyrighted audio can violate a platform's Terms of Service.
26	
27	The ACR backend (chord-extractor + the Chordino Vamp plugin) is NOT a declared
28	dependency because its native plugin doesn't install cleanly everywhere
29	(notably macOS). If it's missing, this script downloads the audio, tells you the
30	wav path, prints exact install guidance, and exits — it degrades, it doesn't
31	crash.
32	
33	Exit codes:
34	  0  draft ChordPro emitted
35	  1  invalid arguments
36	  2  input not found
37	  3  ACR backend unavailable (audio may still have been downloaded — see stderr)
38	  4  audio download / decode failure
39	"""
40	from __future__ import annotations
41	
42	import argparse
43	import re
44	import sys
45	import tempfile
46	from pathlib import Path
47	
48	LRC_TS = re.compile(r"\[(\d+):(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\]")
49	
50	
51	def log(msg: str) -> None:
52	    """Diagnostics -> stderr."""
53	    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
54	
55	
56	def make_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
57	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
58	        prog="audio-to-chords.py",
59	        description="Best-effort link/audio -> draft ChordPro (yt-dlp + chord-extractor).",
60	        epilog=(
61	            "Examples:\n"
62	            '  uv run audio-to-chords.py --dry-run "https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ"\n'
63	            "  uv run audio-to-chords.py -o draft.cho song.wav\n"
64	            '  uv run audio-to-chords.py --lrc song.lrc --title "Hello" song.wav\n'
65	        ),
66	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
67	    )
68	    p.add_argument("input", help="A URL (YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud) or a local audio file.")
69	    p.add_argument("-o", "--output", help="Write ChordPro here instead of stdout.")
70	    p.add_argument("--lrc", help="Optional .lrc (synced lyrics) to align chords onto.")
71	    p.add_argument("--title", help="Song title for the {title:} directive.")
72	    p.add_argument("--artist", help="Artist for the {artist:} directive.")
73	    p.add_argument(
74	        "--dry-run",
75	        action="store_true",
76	        help="Print the plan (no download, no analysis), then exit.",
77	    )
78	    return p
79	
80	
81	def is_url(s: str) -> bool:
82	    return s.startswith("http://") or s.startswith("https://")
83	
84	
85	def download_audio(url: str, outdir: Path) -> tuple[Path, dict]:
86	    """Download bestaudio and convert to wav via yt-dlp + ffmpeg."""
87	    import yt_dlp  # declared dependency
88	
89	    opts = {
90	        "format": "bestaudio/best",
91	        "outtmpl": str(outdir / "%(title)s.%(ext)s"),
92	        "postprocessors": [
93	            {"key": "FFmpegExtractAudio", "preferredcodec": "wav"}
94	        ],
95	        "quiet": True,
96	        "no_warnings": True,
97	    }
98	    with yt_dlp.YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
99	        info = ydl.extract_info(url, download=True)
100	        base = Path(ydl.prepare_filename(info))
101	    wav = base.with_suffix(".wav")
102	    if not wav.exists():
103	        # Fall back to whatever the postprocessor produced.
104	        candidates = sorted(outdir.glob("*.wav"))
105	        if candidates:
106	            wav = candidates[0]
107	    return wav, info
108	
109	
110	def extract_chords(wav: Path) -> list[tuple[float, str]]:
111	    """Run chord-extractor/Chordino. Raises RuntimeError with guidance if the
112	    backend isn't usable, so main() can degrade gracefully."""
113	    try:
114	        from chord_extractor.extractors import Chordino
115	    except ImportError as exc:
116	        raise RuntimeError(
117	            "chord-extractor is not installed.\n"
118	            "  Install (Linux, turnkey):  uv pip install chord-extractor\n"
119	            "  macOS/Windows also need the NNLS-Chroma Vamp plugin + VAMP_PATH,\n"
120	            "  or use `sonic-annotator` / a Linux container.\n"
121	            "  Details: references/audio-to-chords.md"
122	        ) from exc
123	
124	    try:
125	        chordino = Chordino(roll_on=1)
126	        raw = chordino.extract(str(wav))
127	    except Exception as exc:  # Vamp plugin missing at runtime, decode error, etc.
128	        raise RuntimeError(
129	            f"Chordino failed to analyze the audio ({exc}).\n"
130	            "  This usually means the NNLS-Chroma Vamp plugin isn't installed or\n"
131	            "  VAMP_PATH isn't set. See references/audio-to-chords.md for setup,\n"
132	            "  or run `sonic-annotator -d vamp:nnls-chroma:chordino:simplechord`\n"
133	            "  on the wav manually."
134	        ) from exc
135	
136	    changes: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
137	    for item in raw:
138	        chord = getattr(item, "chord", None)
139	        ts = getattr(item, "timestamp", None)
140	        if chord is None and isinstance(item, (list, tuple)) and len(item) >= 2:
141	            chord, ts = item[0], item[1]
142	        if chord is None:
143	            continue
144	        changes.append((float(ts or 0.0), str(chord)))
145	    changes.sort(key=lambda c: c[0])
146	    return changes
147	
148	
149	def dedupe(changes: list[tuple[float, str]]) -> list[tuple[float, str]]:
150	    out: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
151	    for ts, ch in changes:
152	        if not out or out[-1][1] != ch:
153	            out.append((ts, ch))
154	    return out
155	
156	
157	def chord_at(t: float, changes: list[tuple[float, str]]) -> str | None:
158	    cur: str | None = None
159	    for ts, ch in changes:
160	        if ts <= t:
161	            cur = ch
162	        else:
163	            break
164	    if cur in (None, "N", "NC", "N.C."):
165	        return None
166	    return cur
167	
168	
169	def parse_lrc(text: str) -> list[tuple[float, str]]:
170	    lines: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
171	    for raw in text.splitlines():
172	        stamps = LRC_TS.findall(raw)
173	        content = LRC_TS.sub("", raw).strip()
174	        for mm, ss in stamps:
175	            lines.append((int(mm) * 60 + float(ss), content))
176	    lines.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
177	    return lines
178	
179	
180	def mmss(t: float) -> str:
181	    return f"{int(t) // 60:02d}:{int(t) % 60:02d}"
182	
183	
184	def build_chordpro(
185	    changes: list[tuple[float, str]],
186	    lrc_text: str | None,
187	    title: str | None,
188	    artist: str | None,
189	) -> str:
190	    changes = dedupe(changes)
191	    out: list[str] = []
192	    if title:
193	        out.append(f"{{title: {title}}}")
194	    if artist:
195	        out.append(f"{{artist: {artist}}}")
196	    out.append("{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}")
197	    out.append("")
198	
199	    if lrc_text:
200	        lyric_lines = parse_lrc(lrc_text)
201	        if lyric_lines:
202	            out.append("{start_of_verse}")
203	            for t, content in lyric_lines:
204	                ch = chord_at(t, changes)
205	                prefix = f"[{ch}]" if ch else ""
206	                out.append(f"{prefix}{content}" if content else (prefix or ""))
207	            out.append("{end_of_verse}")
208	            out.append("")
209	
210	    # Always include the raw chord timeline so the user can correct placement.
211	    out.append("{comment: Detected chord timeline (mm:ss → chord)}")
212	    out.append("{start_of_tab}")
213	    if changes:
214	        for t, ch in changes:
215	            out.append(f"{mmss(t)}  {ch}")
216	    else:
217	        out.append("(no chords detected)")
218	    out.append("{end_of_tab}")
219	    out.append("")
220	    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"
221	
222	
223	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
224	    args = make_parser().parse_args(argv)
225	
226	    src_is_url = is_url(args.input)
227	    if not src_is_url and not Path(args.input).exists():
228	        log(f"input not found: {args.input}")
229	        return 2
230	
231	    if args.dry_run:
232	        log("[dry-run] plan:")
233	        if src_is_url:
234	            log(f"  1. yt-dlp download bestaudio -> wav  ({args.input})")
235	        else:
236	            log(f"  1. use local audio file  ({args.input})")
237	        log("  2. chord-extractor/Chordino -> chord timeline")
238	        if args.lrc:
239	            log(f"  3. align chords onto lyric lines from {args.lrc}")
240	        log("  4. emit ChordPro with AUTO-GENERATED header")
241	        log("Reminder: personal-use / local only; respect platform ToS + copyright.")
242	        return 0
243	
244	    tmpdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="chordpro-audio-"))
245	    if src_is_url:
246	        log(f"downloading audio with yt-dlp -> {tmpdir} …")
247	        try:
248	            wav, info = download_audio(args.input, tmpdir)
249	        except Exception as exc:  # DownloadError, missing ffmpeg, etc.
250	            log(f"audio download failed: {exc}")
251	            log("Ensure yt-dlp and ffmpeg are available; some tracks are gated "
252	                "(try --cookies-from-browser via yt-dlp directly).")
253	            return 4
254	        if not args.title:
255	            args.title = info.get("track") or info.get("title")
256	        if not args.artist:
257	            args.artist = info.get("artist") or info.get("uploader")
258	        log(f"audio: {wav}")
259	    else:
260	        wav = Path(args.input)
261	
262	    try:
263	        changes = extract_chords(wav)
264	    except RuntimeError as exc:
265	        log(str(exc))
266	        log(f"The audio is available at: {wav}")
267	        return 3
268	
269	    log(f"detected {len(dedupe(changes))} chord changes")
270	
271	    lrc_text = None
272	    if args.lrc:
273	        lrc_path = Path(args.lrc)
274	        if not lrc_path.exists():
275	            log(f"--lrc file not found: {args.lrc} (continuing without lyrics)")
276	        else:
277	            lrc_text = lrc_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
278	
279	    cho = build_chordpro(changes, lrc_text, args.title, args.artist)
280	
281	    if args.output:
282	        Path(args.output).write_text(cho, encoding="utf-8")
283	        log(f"wrote {args.output}")
284	        log("Next: review + correct, then validate with scripts/validate-cho.sh")
285	    else:
286	        sys.stdout.write(cho)
287	    return 0
288	
289	
290	if __name__ == "__main__":
291	    sys.exit(main())
292

8	"""fetch-lyrics.py — Fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (free, no API key).
9	
10	LRCLIB is the default lyrics source for this skill: open, key-less,
11	cross-platform, and it returns time-synced .lrc when available. Lyrics (the
12	data) go to stdout or --output; diagnostics go to stderr.
13	
14	Run with uv (self-contained via PEP 723 inline metadata):
15	
16	    uv run fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
17	    uv run fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..." -o out.txt
18	
19	Other sources (Musixmatch, NetEase, QQ, Genius, Mojim) are documented in
20	references/lyrics-sources.md — this script intentionally ships only the open
21	LRCLIB path and does not scrape.
22	
23	Exit codes:
24	  0  lyrics found and emitted
25	  1  invalid arguments
26	  3  no matching lyrics found
27	  4  network / API error
28	"""
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	import argparse
32	import sys
33	
34	import httpx
35	
36	LRCLIB = "https://lrclib.net/api"
37	UA = "chordpro-skill/1.0 (agent-skills; +https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills)"
38	
39	
40	def log(msg: str) -> None:
41	    """Diagnostics -> stderr."""
42	    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
43	
44	
45	def make_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
46	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
47	        prog="fetch-lyrics.py",
48	        description="Fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced .lrc by default, --plain for text).",
49	        epilog=(
50	            "Examples:\n"
51	            '  uv run fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295\n'
52	            '  uv run fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "周杰倫" --track "晴天"\n'
53	        ),
54	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
55	    )
56	    p.add_argument("--artist", required=True, help="Artist / performer name.")
57	    p.add_argument("--track", required=True, help="Track / song title.")
58	    p.add_argument("--album", help="Album name (improves exact-match on /get).")
59	    p.add_argument(
60	        "--duration",
61	        type=int,
62	        help="Track duration in seconds (helps disambiguate on /get and /search).",
63	    )
64	    p.add_argument(
65	        "--plain",
66	        action="store_true",
67	        help="Return plain text instead of the synced .lrc.",
68	    )
69	    p.add_argument("-o", "--output", help="Write lyrics to this file instead of stdout.")
70	    p.add_argument(
71	        "--dry-run",
72	        action="store_true",
73	        help="Print the requests that would be made, then exit.",
74	    )
75	    return p
76	
77	
78	def _emit(text: str, output: str | None) -> None:
79	    if output:
80	        with open(output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
81	            fh.write(text.rstrip("\n") + "\n")
82	        log(f"wrote {output} ({len(text.splitlines())} lines)")
83	    else:
84	        sys.stdout.write(text.rstrip("\n") + "\n")
85	
86	
87	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
88	    args = make_parser().parse_args(argv)
89	
90	    get_params: dict[str, object] = {
91	        "artist_name": args.artist,
92	        "track_name": args.track,
93	    }
94	    if args.album:
95	        get_params["album_name"] = args.album
96	    if args.duration:
97	        get_params["duration"] = args.duration
98	
99	    if args.dry_run:
100	        log(f"[dry-run] GET {LRCLIB}/get params={get_params}")
101	        log(
102	            f"[dry-run] fallback GET {LRCLIB}/search "
103	            f"params={{'artist_name': {args.artist!r}, 'track_name': {args.track!r}}}"
104	        )
105	        return 0
106	
107	    try:
108	        with httpx.Client(headers={"User-Agent": UA}, timeout=20.0) as client:
109	            rec: dict | None = None
110	            resp = client.get(f"{LRCLIB}/get", params=get_params)
111	            if resp.status_code == 200:
112	                rec = resp.json()
113	                log(f"exact match: {rec.get('artistName')} – {rec.get('trackName')}")
114	            elif resp.status_code == 404:
115	                log("exact /get miss; trying /search…")
116	                sresp = client.get(
117	                    f"{LRCLIB}/search",
118	                    params={"artist_name": args.artist, "track_name": args.track},
119	                )
120	                sresp.raise_for_status()
121	                results = sresp.json() or []
122	                if not results:
123	                    log("no results from LRCLIB search")
124	                    return 3
125	                if args.duration:
126	                    results.sort(
127	                        key=lambda r: abs((r.get("duration") or 0) - args.duration)
128	                    )
129	                rec = results[0]
130	                log(
131	                    f"best search match: {rec.get('artistName')} – "
132	                    f"{rec.get('trackName')} ({rec.get('duration')}s)"
133	                )
134	            else:
135	                resp.raise_for_status()
136	    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
137	        log(f"LRCLIB request failed: {exc}")
138	        return 4
139	
140	    if rec is None:
141	        log("no matching lyrics found")
142	        return 3
143	    if rec.get("instrumental"):
144	        log("LRCLIB marks this track as instrumental — no lyrics available.")
145	        return 3
146	
147	    synced = rec.get("syncedLyrics")
148	    plain = rec.get("plainLyrics")
149	
150	    if args.plain:
151	        text = plain or ""
152	        if not text:
153	            log("no plain lyrics available for this track")
154	            return 3
155	    else:
156	        text = synced or ""
157	        if not text:
158	            log("no synced .lrc available; falling back to plain text (--plain)")
159	            text = plain or ""
160	        if not text:
161	            log("no lyrics (synced or plain) available for this track")
162	            return 3
163	
164	    _emit(text, args.output)
165	    return 0

```md
# Never Gonna Give You Up — Chord Chart

**Artist:** Rick Astley
**Source:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ
**Original key:** A♭ major
**Feel:** 4/4, ~113 BPM, upbeat pop

> Note: This chart was reconstructed from general musical knowledge, NOT
> from analyzing the audio (per instructions, the audio was not downloaded).
> Treat chords/timing as a solid starting point and verify by ear.

## Chords used (A♭ major / original key)

| Chord | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| A♭    | A♭ C E♭ |
| B♭m   | B♭ D♭ F |
| Cm    | C E♭ G |
| D♭    | D♭ F A♭ |
| E♭    | E♭ G B♭ |
| Fm    | F A♭ C |

Roman numerals in A♭:  A♭ = I,  B♭m = ii,  Cm = iii,  D♭ = IV,  E♭ = V,  Fm = vi.

The chorus is the famous **I–V–vi–IV**: A♭ – E♭ – Fm – D♭.

## Easier key for guitar (Capo)

Play the **G-major shapes** below and put a **capo on fret 1** to sound in
the original A♭. Shapes: G, Am, Bm, C, D, Em (= A♭, B♭m, Cm, D♭, E♭, Fm).

---

## Structure

Intro → Verse 1 → Pre-Chorus → Chorus → Verse 2 → Pre-Chorus → Chorus →
Instrumental → Bridge → Chorus (x2 to fade)

### Intro
\```
| A♭  B♭m | D♭   E♭ |   (x2)
\```

### Verse
\```
A♭              B♭m
We're no strangers to love
D♭                    E♭
You know the rules and so do I
Cm                       Fm
A full commitment's what I'm thinking of
D♭        E♭          A♭
You wouldn't get this from any other guy
\```
(second half of each verse repeats the same 4-chord pattern)

### Pre-Chorus
\```
Cm               Fm
I just wanna tell you how I'm feeling
D♭            E♭
Gotta make you understand
\```

### Chorus
\```
A♭      E♭     Fm      D♭
Never gonna give you up
A♭      E♭          D♭
Never gonna let you down
A♭      E♭       Fm        D♭
Never gonna run around and desert you
A♭      E♭     Fm      D♭
Never gonna make you cry
A♭      E♭         D♭
Never gonna say goodbye
A♭      E♭        Fm      D♭
Never gonna tell a lie and hurt you
\```

### Bridge
\```
| D♭  E♭ | Fm | D♭  E♭ | Fm |
Give you up, give you up... (build back into Chorus)
\```

---

A ChordPro (`.cho`) version of this chart is in
`never-gonna-give-you-up.chopro` for use with ChordPro / OnSong / etc.

```

How it was made: I used the ChordPro CLI (`chordpro`, core 6.101.0) that was installed under `~/perl5`. The binary couldn't find its own module tree out of the box, so I pointed Perl at it with `PERL5LIB=~/perl5/lib/perl5`, then ran it with `--transpose=2`. ## (2) Commands run

\```bash
# Locate + inspect the chordpro binary
ls ~/perl5/bin/                              # found: chordpro (a Perl script)
~/perl5/bin/chordpro --version               # failed: Can't locate ChordPro.pm in @INC

# Find the module tree the binary needs
find ~/perl5 -name ChordPro.pm               # -> ~/perl5/lib/perl5/ChordPro.pm

# Fix the include path (module lives in lib/perl5, binary only searched lib)
export PERL5LIB=~/perl5/lib/perl5
~/perl5/bin/chordpro --version               # -> This is ChordPro core 6.101.0

# See available transpose / output flags
~/perl5/bin/chordpro --help | grep -iE 'transpose|output|pdf'

# 1) Emit a transposed ChordPro source (+2 semitones)
~/perl5/bin/chordpro --transpose=2 --generate=ChordPro \
  -o outputs/eval-2-transposed.cho fixtures/eval-2-input.cho

# 2) Render the transposed PDF (+2 semitones)
~/perl5/bin/chordpro --transpose=2 \
  -o outputs/eval-2-transposed.pdf fixtures/eval-2-input.cho

# Verify the PDF text (via pypdf) shows A / E / D chords
uv run --with pypdf python3 -c "from pypdf import PdfReader; print(PdfReader('outputs/eval-2-transposed.pdf').pages[0].extract_text())"

# RESULT

## (1) Final message to the user (verbatim)

幫你把王力宏〈落葉歸根〉整理成一份 ChordPro 吉他譜了，檔案在：
`.../without_skill/outputs/落葉歸根.chordpro`

**先說明一個取捨：** 傳統 ChordPro 譜會把和弦逐字疊在**完整歌詞**上，但〈落葉歸根〉的歌詞仍在版權保護內，我不便把整首歌詞照抄進檔案。所以我做的是一份 **「和弦進行譜 / lead sheet」**——涵蓋曲式結構、每小節和弦進行、和弦指型圖與右手節奏建議（這些是樂理層面的資訊），歌詞的部分請你對照下方授權譜站，把每一句對齊到對應的小節，就能邊看邊彈唱。

**譜面重點**
- **調性**：原曲音高約 G#/Ab。此譜以 **G 調指型**記寫，夾 **Capo 1** 即貼近原調；不夾 Capo 直接彈就是低半音的 G 調。
- **拍號 / 速度**：4/4，抒情 ballad，♩≈72（慢拍感；有些測速庫會回報約 124，那是 double-time 的同一速度）。
- **曲式**：Intro → 主歌 → 導歌(Pre-Chorus) → 副歌 → 主歌 → 導歌 → 副歌 → Bridge → 副歌 → Outro。
- **用到的和弦**（共 15 個）：G、D/F#、Em、Bm7、C、G/B、Am7、D、Dm/F、E、B、A/C#、Cm，加上副歌尾段的經過和弦 Em/Eb、Em/D（低音 E→D#→D→C# 級進下行，上方保持 Em 指型；初學者可整段用 Em 帶過）。
- **主歌進行**：G – D/F# – Em – Bm7 – C – G/B – Am7 – D
- **導歌進行**：Dm/F – E – C – B ／ Em – A/C# – Am7 – D
- **右手**：主奏用分解和弦（拇指根音＋往上分解）；副歌想加強可用慢速刷法 ↓ ↓↑ ↑↓↑。

檔案已是標準 ChordPro 格式（含 `{define:}` 指型圖與 `{start_of_chorus}` 等段落標記），可直接丟進 ChordPro / SongBook 等 App 渲染成六線和弦圖。

想要的話我可以再幫你：(a) 轉成不夾 Capo 的把位、或改 Capo 3 的版本；(b) 把分解指法寫成六線譜(TAB)；(c) 產生可列印的 HTML/PDF。

**資料來源（和弦與曲目資訊）：**
- [落葉歸根 – 王力宏 – Chord4](https://chord4.com/zh-hant/tabs/12061)（和弦進行、拍號）
- [落葉歸根 吉他譜 – kanpu8](https://kanpu8.com/chords/falling-leaf-returns-to-root/)（原調 G#、Capo 1 / G 調指型）
- [改變自己 (Change Me) – 王力宏官方專輯頁](https://wangleehom.com/tw/album/change-me/)（專輯 / 年份）
- [落葉歸根 簡譜與演奏指南 – 百度文庫](https://wenku.baidu.com/view/7b82c00510791711cc7931b765ce0508763275f2.html)（ballad ~72 BPM）

# RESULT

## (1) Final message to the user (verbatim)

幫你做好王力宏〈落葉歸根〉的 ChordPro 吉他彈唱譜了 🎸

**檔案**（都在 outputs/ 資料夾）
- `luoye-guigen.cho` — ChordPro 主譜（已通過 `chordpro --strict` 驗證，0 warnings）
- `luoye-guigen.html` — 可直接用瀏覽器開的排版版本
- `luoye-guigen.lrc` — LRCLIB 抓下來的時間軸歌詞（原始素材）
- `luoye-guigen.txt` — 純文字歌詞

**這份譜的重點**
- **調性 / Capo**：原曲是 **Ab (G#) 大調**。此譜用 **G 調和弦指法**，**Capo 夾第 1 格**就還原成原調、跟著唱片彈。若不想夾 Capo，直接彈也行，只是會比原曲低半音。
- **拍速**：約 72 BPM、4/4 拍的抒情慢歌。
- **結構**：前奏 → 主歌1 → 導歌 → 副歌 → 間奏轉句 → 主歌2 → 導歌 → 副歌 → 橋段 → 尾段副歌。
- **常用和弦**：G、D/F#、Em、Bm7、C、G/B、Am7、D，副歌另有 B、A/C#、Cm；間奏用了經典下行 line cliché `Em → Emmaj7 → Em7 → A/C#`。

**要老實說的地方（lyrics-only 流程）**
- **歌詞**是從 LRCLIB 精確比對抓下來的，可信度高。
- **和弦是「建議編配」**：我依常見的吉他版本（Capo 1 / G 調）整理，不是從音檔自動辨識來的，所以請一定**對照原曲錄音再微調**。其中**導歌（命運的安排…）和間奏轉句**的和弦不確定性最高，最需要你自己聽過確認；**橋段（但願陪你找回…）**我是按和聲走向合理推的，也請核對。

**怎麼用**
\```bash
# 需要先載入 chordpro 環境
export PERL5LIB="$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5"; export PATH="$HOME/perl5/bin:$PATH"

# 轉成 PDF（中文需先在 config 掛 CJK 字型，否則中文可能不顯示）
chordpro -o luoye-guigen.pdf luoye-guigen.cho
# 移調：例如往上 2 個半音
chordpro -x 2 -o up.cho luoye-guigen.cho
\```

要不要我幫你：(a) 把它移到某個不用 Capo 的調（例如 C 或 A）？(b) 加上前奏／間奏的六線譜指法？(c) 補上和弦圖 `{define}`？跟我說一聲就好。

參考來源（和弦與調性核對）：
- [落葉歸根 - 王力宏 - Chord4](https://chord4.com/zh-hant/tabs/12061)
- [落叶归根 C调和弦级数谱 - 琴魂网](https://www.qinhun.com/pu/43426.html)（標原調 G#/Ab，Capo 1 還原）
- [落葉歸根 和弦 - kanpu8](https://kanpu8.com/chords/falling-leaf-returns-to-root/)
- 歌詞來源：[LRCLIB](https://lrclib.net)（王力宏 – 落葉歸根，exact match）

```md
# Finding existing chord charts online

Read this when the user wants chords for a **known/popular song** (by title, by
lyrics, or from a link) and hasn't pasted chords or supplied audio. For most
songs people ask about, **a human-made chart already exists on the web** — and it
is usually *more accurate* than machine audio→chord extraction (`audio-to-chords.py`,
~80%). So the reliable first move is: search chart sites → adapt the chart to
ChordPro → validate. Fall back to audio ACR or interactive fill only when no
chart is found.

This is the router's highest-value path for "make me a chord sheet for `<song>`",
and it's what actually happens in practice — treat existing charts as the
default source of chords, not an afterthought.

## The workflow

1. **Search.** `WebSearch` for the song + a chart keyword in the right language:
   - EN: `"<artist> <title>" chords`, `... ultimate guitar`, `... chordpro`
   - 中文: `<歌手> <歌名> 吉他谱`, `... 和弦`, `... 弹唱谱`, `... 简谱`
2. **Fetch.** `WebFetch` the most promising result and pull the **chords-over-lyrics**
   block (chord symbols on their own line above each lyric line).
3. **Adapt.** If it's chords-over-lyrics text, run it through `chordpro --a2crd`
   (see `cli-and-rendering.md`) — that's exactly its input format. If it's already
   inline or a chart, transcribe it into the ChordPro template.
4. **Validate + caption.** Run `scripts/validate-cho.sh`. Add a `{comment:}` noting
   the source and that it's a *published arrangement to verify against the
   recording* (capo/key can differ between charts). Do **not** stamp the
   machine-extraction `AUTO-GENERATED` header — this isn't ACR — but do stay honest
   that a web chart is one person's arrangement, not ground truth.

## Where the charts live

Coverage and format vary; try a couple. **Text (chords-over-lyrics)** sites feed
straight into `a2crd`; **image** charts (many 吉他谱/简谱 scans) need manual
transcription (no reliable OMR). Auto-generated sites are effectively ACR — same
~80% caveat.

**Chinese / Taiwan (great for C-pop like the 落葉歸根 case):**
- **91譜 / 91pu** — `91pu.com.tw` — large Taiwan library of ready 吉他谱/弹唱谱; often the fastest hit for Mandarin songs.
- **Chord4 / 和弦网** — `chord4.com` — chords-over-lyrics, capo/key noted (used by the eval runs).
- **弹唱谱 / 简谱 hubs** — `kanpu8`, `qupu123`, `中国曲谱网 (qupu.com)`, `17jita (17吉他网)`, `jitaba/jitapu` — mix of text and image; simplified-character search often finds more.
- **魔鏡歌詞 / Mojim** — `mojim.com` — mostly lyrics, some chords; good for confirming lyrics.

**Western / global:**
- **Ultimate Guitar** — `ultimate-guitar.com` — the largest; use the **"Chords"** tab (chords-over-lyrics) not "Tab". No official API; scrape the page.
- **e-chords**, **Chordie**, **AZChords** — chords-over-lyrics.
- **Songsterr** — public API for tabs/chords (`songsterr.com/a/wsa/api-tabs-a26570`).
- **Chordu / Chordify / GuitarTuna** — **auto-generated from audio** → treat as ACR-quality (~80%, verify), not human-checked.

## Format taxonomy (what you'll get back)

| Format | How to use it | Reliability |
|---|---|---|
| Chords-over-lyrics text | `chordpro --a2crd` → clean up → validate | High (human-made) |
| Inline / chord chart | transcribe into the ChordPro template | High |
| Guitar tab (6-line) | embed in a `{start_of_tab}` block; or use for riffs only | High for riffs |
| 简谱 (numbered) / image scan | manual transcription; no reliable OMR | Low (tedious) |
| Auto-generated (chordu/chordify) | same as ACR — a draft to verify | ~80% |

## Legality (surface it, don't bury it)

These charts are user-contributed arrangements; the underlying songs are usually
copyrighted. Keep it **personal-use and local**, don't redistribute the fetched
chart or lyrics commercially, and cite the source in a `{comment:}`. Prefer this
route over downloading audio — it avoids the platform-ToS problem entirely — but
the copyright of the song itself still applies to any lyrics you embed.

```

3	description: Author, convert, validate, render, and transpose ChordPro chord sheets, and build one for a song from an existing online chart, lyrics, or audio. Use when the user mentions ChordPro or .cho/.crd/.pro files, `[C]lyric` inline chords or `{title:}`/`{start_of_chorus}` directives, the `chordpro`/`a2crd` CLI, converting chords-over-lyrics (Ultimate Guitar/OnSong) text, making a guitar chord sheet for a song by name, or extracting chords from a YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud link or mp3/wav. References chordpro.org.
4	---
5	
6	# chordpro
7	
8	Produce and work with [ChordPro](https://www.chordpro.org/) chord sheets — the
9	plain-text format where chords live inline in the lyrics as `[C]like [G]this`.
10	This skill is a **router that degrades gracefully**: it picks the most reliable
11	workflow for whatever the user actually has (a `.cho` file, a chords-over-lyrics
12	paste, bare lyrics, an audio file, or just a song title) and every path ends by
13	**validating** the output. It is honest about the one hard part — extracting
14	chords from raw audio is an ~80%-accurate *draft*, never an oracle — and falls
15	back to interactive, fill-in-the-gaps assistance instead of pretending otherwise.
16	
17	## When to use
18	
19	- User names **ChordPro** / `.cho` / `.crd` / `.chopro` / `.pro`, inline
20	  `[C]lyric` chords, or `{title:}` / `{start_of_chorus}` / `{soc}` directives.
21	- Convert an existing sheet: **chords-over-lyrics** text (Ultimate Guitar, OnSong,
22	  a lyric with chord letters on the line above) → ChordPro.
23	- Render / transpose / validate a `.cho` with the **`chordpro`** or **`a2crd`** CLI.
24	- "Make a chord sheet for <song>" starting from **lyrics only**, or from a
25	  **YouTube / Bilibili / SoundCloud link** or an **mp3 / wav** file.
26	- Ask about **lyrics sources** (Mojim/魔鏡, KKBOX, Musixmatch, LRCLIB, Genius,
27	  NetEase, QQ Music) — which give time-synced `.lrc` vs plain text.
28	
29	## When NOT to use
30	
31	- **Engraving staff notation** (notes on a staff, MusicXML / MIDI / LilyPond /
32	  MuseScore output) — ChordPro is lyrics+chords, not a score. Hand off to a
33	  notation tool. (ChordPro *can* embed ABC/LilyPond fragments — see the format
34	  reference — but it is not an engraver.)
35	- **OMR from a scanned score image** (photo/PDF of printed sheet music → notes)
36	  is out of scope; there is no reliable open path. Offer manual transcription
37	  into ChordPro instead, and say so plainly.
38	
39	## Authoritative sources
40	
41	- Format + directives + CLI: **https://www.chordpro.org/** (link, don't
42	  paraphrase from memory — the directive set evolves).
43	- Source / releases: **https://github.com/ChordPro/chordpro**.
44	
45	## The router — pick the workflow by what the user has
46	
47	| User has… | Do this | Reliability |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| A `.cho`/`.crd`/`.pro` file | Render / transpose / **validate** via `chordpro` CLI | High |
50	| **Chords-over-lyrics** text (UG/OnSong) | `a2crd` → light manual cleanup → validate | High |
51	| A **known song** (title / lyrics / a link) and no chords yet | **Search existing chord charts online** → adapt to ChordPro (often via `a2crd`) → validate. See `references/chord-tab-sources.md` | Med–High (**best first move**) |
52	| **Lyrics only**, no chart found | Fetch/confirm lyrics → **interactively** fill chords (propose from key, ask the user to confirm/correct) | Medium (human-in-loop) |
53	| An **audio file or link**, want a machine draft | `scripts/audio-to-chords.py` → *draft* with `AUTO-GENERATED` header → human correction | ~80% (last resort) |
54	
55	Prefer the highest row that fits. Two rules that matter: don't jump to the audio
56	pipeline when the user already pasted chords (`a2crd` is faster and correct); and
57	for a **named/popular song, search for an existing human-made chart first** — it's
58	usually more accurate than audio ACR and sidesteps the download-ToS problem
59	entirely.
60	
61	## ChordPro cheat-sheet + output template
62	
63	- **Extensions**: `.cho` (recommended), also `.crd` `.chopro` `.chord` `.pro`.
64	  Plain UTF-8. `#` starts a comment line; blank lines separate blocks.
65	- **Inline chords**: `[C]` immediately before the syllable it sits over —
66	  `Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot`. Annotations (non-chords): `[*softly]`.
67	- **Metadata**: `{title:}`/`{t:}`, `{subtitle:}`/`{st:}`, `{artist:}`,
68	  `{composer:}`, `{album:}`, `{year:}`, `{key:}`, `{tempo:}`, `{time:}`, `{capo:}`.
69	- **Environments** (long / short): chorus `{start_of_chorus}`/`{soc}` …
70	  `{end_of_chorus}`/`{eoc}`; verse `{sov}`…`{eov}`; bridge `{sob}`…`{eob}`;
71	  tab (monospaced, chords NOT parsed) `{sot}`…`{eot}`. Recall a chorus with
72	  `{chorus}`. Comments: `{comment:}`/`{c:}`.
73	
74	Emit this shape — metadata block → environments/comments → verses/choruses:
75	
76	```
77	{title: Swing Low Sweet Chariot}
78	{artist: Traditional}
79	{key: G}
80	{tempo: 90}
81	{time: 4/4}
82	
83	{comment: Intro}
84	[G] [C] [G] [D]
85	
86	{start_of_chorus: Chorus}
87	Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot,
88	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
89	{end_of_chorus}
90	
91	{start_of_verse: Verse 1}
92	I [G]looked over Jordan, and [C]what did I [G]see,
93	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
94	{end_of_verse}
95	
96	{chorus}
97	```
98	
99	Full directive set (chord `{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup, ABC/LilyPond
100	blocks, `x_` custom namespace) → read `references/chordpro-format.md`.
101	
102	## The `chordpro` / `a2crd` CLI (essentials)
103	
104	The official tool is a Perl program (CPAN dist **`App::Music::ChordPro`**). Current
105	6.x releases install the **`chordpro`** command; the chords-over-lyrics importer
106	is `chordpro --a2crd` (a standalone `a2crd` binary shipped in older releases and
107	may be absent — prefer `chordpro --a2crd`).
108	
109	```bash
110	# Install (macOS — there is NO official Homebrew formula; use CPAN)
111	brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro
112	# If `chordpro` then errors "Can't locate ChordPro.pm", activate local::lib once:
113	eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"   # add to ~/.zshrc to persist
114	
115	# Render
116	chordpro -o song.pdf song.cho          # PDF (format inferred from extension)
117	chordpro --generate=HTML -o song.html song.cho
118	
119	# Transpose (N semitones; suffix s/f forces sharp/flat spelling)
120	chordpro -x 2  -o up.pdf   song.cho
121	chordpro -x -3f -o down.pdf song.cho
122	
123	# Convert chords-over-lyrics text -> ChordPro (the official importer)
124	chordpro --a2crd input.txt -o song.cho
125	```
126	
127	Install-per-platform, generators, config JSON, songbook `--toc`, and `a2crd`
128	heuristic tuning → read `references/cli-and-rendering.md`.
129	
130	## Verify loop — never hand back an unvalidated `.cho`
131	
132	Every generated or edited file goes through the parser before you present it:
133	
134	```bash
135	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # wraps the command below; PASS/FAIL + warnings
136	# equivalently:
137	chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o - song.cho   # exit 0 + no stderr warnings = valid
138	```
139	
140	To auto-normalize to canonical form (fix spacing, round-trip directives):
141	`chordpro --generate=ChordPro -o song.cho song.cho`. If `chordpro` isn't
142	installed, the script prints the install one-liner — say so and offer to proceed
143	without rendering (the format is still human-checkable).
144	
145	## Finding existing chord charts (the usual first move)
146	
147	For a named/popular song, a human-made chart almost always already exists online
148	and beats audio extraction on accuracy. Search chart sites, pull the
149	**chords-over-lyrics** block, run it through `chordpro --a2crd`, then validate:
150	
151	```bash
152	# 1. search (中文: 吉他谱/和弦/弹唱谱; EN: chords / ultimate guitar)
153	# 2. WebFetch the best hit, copy the chords-over-lyrics into chart.txt
154	chordpro --a2crd chart.txt -o song.cho   # 3. convert
155	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # 4. validate
156	```
157	
158	Caption the result with a `{comment:}` naming the source and "published
159	arrangement — verify against the recording (capo/key may differ)". This is *not*
160	machine ACR, so don't use the `AUTO-GENERATED` header — but a web chart is still
161	one person's arrangement, not ground truth. Site catalog (91譜/Chord4/Ultimate
162	Guitar/…), format taxonomy, and legality → read `references/chord-tab-sources.md`.
163	
164	## Generating from audio / links — the fallback when no chart exists
165	
166	This is the shakiest path — reach for it only when no existing chart is available.
167	
168	**Set expectations first**: open automatic chord recognition tops out around **78–80% on simple major/minor pop**
169	and drops sharply on 7ths, extended/jazz chords, key changes, and quiet or dense
170	mixes; inversions/slash chords are unreliable; and it cannot know the capo a
171	guitarist used. Treat the result as a **draft to correct**, not a transcription.
172	
173	```bash
174	# Best-effort turnkey: link or local file -> draft ChordPro
175	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py --dry-run "https://youtu.be/..."   # show the plan first
176	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py -o draft.cho "https://youtu.be/..."
177	```
178	
179	The script downloads audio with `yt-dlp` (YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud) and runs
180	`chord-extractor`/Chordino. Its output **must** carry the
181	`{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}` header. On macOS the
182	Chordino Vamp plugin often isn't installed; the script detects that and prints
183	exact install guidance + manual alternatives instead of crashing — relay that to
184	the user rather than silently failing. Tool comparison, beat/key detection, and
185	commercial escape hatches (Moises/Songsterr have APIs; Chordify/Chord AI/Ultimate
186	Guitar don't) → read `references/audio-to-chords.md`.
187	
188	**Legal**: only process content the user owns or has the right to use, for
189	personal use, locally; downloading copyrighted audio can violate a platform's
190	ToS. Surface this — don't bury it.
191	
192	## Lyrics sources
193	
194	Default to **LRCLIB** — free, no API key, returns time-synced `.lrc`:
195	
196	```bash
197	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
198	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..."   # plain text
199	```
200	
201	| Source | Access | Synced `.lrc`? |
202	|---|---|---|
203	| **LRCLIB** | free, no key | **yes** |
204	| Musixmatch | API key; full/synced is paid | yes (paid) |
205	| NetEase / QQ Music | unofficial community APIs | yes (Chinese catalog) |
206	| Genius (`lyricsgenius`) | API token; lyrics scraped from page | no (plain) |
207	| Mojim / 魔鏡 | scrape-only | no (plain) |
208	| KKBOX | partner-gated | n/a |
209	
210	Full comparison, legality, and the LRCLIB API → read `references/lyrics-sources.md`.
211	
212	## Available scripts
213	
214	- **`scripts/validate-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — verify a file parses cleanly
215	  (`chordpro --strict`); PASS/FAIL to stdout, warnings to stderr. Guides install
216	  if `chordpro` is missing. Flags: `--help`.
217	- **`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py`** — fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced `.lrc` default,
218	  `--plain` for text). Self-contained via `uv run`. Flags: `--artist`, `--track`,
219	  `--duration`, `--album`, `--plain`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
220	- **`scripts/audio-to-chords.py`** — best-effort link/audio → draft ChordPro
221	  (`yt-dlp` + `chord-extractor`). Degrades gracefully when the ACR backend is
222	  unavailable. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--lrc`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
223	
224	## Bundled assets
225	
226	Ready-to-open examples + a template under `assets/` (all songs are **public
227	domain**; every `.cho` validates clean with `chordpro --strict`). Use them as
228	copy-paste starting points and few-shot references:
229	
230	- `assets/example-amazing-grace.cho` — simplest real song: metadata + inline chords.
231	- `assets/example-when-the-saints.cho` — chorus/verse structure + `{chorus}` recall.
232	- `assets/example-greensleeves.cho` — feature showcase: `{define}` diagrams, a
233	  `{sot}` tab block, chorus recall, transpose note.
234	- `assets/template-song.cho` — fill-in-the-blanks scaffold (renders as-is); the
235	  starting point for the interactive chord-fill flow.
236	- `assets/example-synced-lyrics.lrc` — sample time-synced `.lrc` (what
237	  `fetch-lyrics.py` returns; feed it to `audio-to-chords.py --lrc`).
238	- `assets/example-a2crd-input.txt` — chords-over-lyrics plain text; convert with
239	  `chordpro --a2crd assets/example-a2crd-input.txt`.
240	
241	## Reference files
242	
243	- `references/chordpro-format.md` — Read **when** hand-authoring or you need a
244	  directive beyond the cheat-sheet (`{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup,
245	  ABC/LilyPond, `x_` custom namespace).
246	- `references/chord-tab-sources.md` — Read **when** you need chords for a named
247	  song and have none: where to find existing charts (91譜/Chord4/Ultimate
248	  Guitar/…), how to adapt them, and the legality.
249	- `references/cli-and-rendering.md` — Read **when** installing, rendering,
250	  transposing, converting with `a2crd`, or validating/normalizing.
251	- `references/audio-to-chords.md` — Read **when** the user wants chords from an
252	  audio file or a link (ACR tool choice, beat/key, limits, escape hatches).
253	- `references/lyrics-sources.md` — Read **when** fetching lyrics (source table,
254	  synced-vs-plain, API-vs-scrape, legality, LRCLIB API).
255	
256	## Gotchas
257	
258	- **macOS has no official Homebrew `chordpro`** — install via CPAN
259	  (`brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`). A signed `.dmg`
260	  GUI exists on GitHub Releases but the CLI is the CPAN route.
261	- **`Can't locate ChordPro.pm in @INC` after cpanm** — cpanm installed into a
262	  `local::lib` (`~/perl5`) that isn't on Perl's path. Activate it:
263	  `eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"` (persist in `~/.zshrc`).
264	- **No standalone `a2crd` in ChordPro 6.x** — use `chordpro --a2crd input.txt`.
265	  Its output needs a human pass (heuristic, column-based chord placement); always
266	  validate and eyeball before rendering.
267	- **Angle brackets `< >` are text markup in ChordPro v6.** Don't put `<...>`
268	  placeholders in lyrics/chords — the parser reads `<b>`/`<i>`-style markup and
269	  floods warnings. Use plain-text placeholders (see `assets/template-song.cho`).
270	- **No official online validator.** chordpro.org hosts docs + a desktop GUI, not
271	  a "try it online" box. Validate locally with the CLI (`validate-cho.sh`).
272	- **Chord accuracy from audio is ~80% at best** on simple pop, worse otherwise.
273	  Never present a machine-extracted sheet without the `AUTO-GENERATED` header and
274	  a "verify chords/key/timing" caveat.
275	- **Auto-generated chart sites are ACR in disguise.** Chordu / Chordify /
276	  GuitarTuna charts are machine-derived (~80%, same caveat) — treat them as drafts,
277	  unlike human-made charts on 91譜 / Chord4 / Ultimate Guitar.
278	- **Detected key is a suggestion.** ACR outputs absolute pitches; key detection
279	  confuses relative major/minor and keys a fifth apart, and enharmonic spelling
280	  (Gb vs F#) is ambiguous. Confirm with the user before committing `{key:}`.
281	- **Chords in `{sot}`…`{eot}` tab blocks are NOT parsed** — that's for ASCII tab.
282	  Use inline `[..]` in verses/choruses; reserve tab blocks for fret diagrams.
283	- **Lyrics/audio ToS.** Prefer LRCLIB (open); most other lyric sources are
284	  scrape-only or paid, and downloading audio has copyright/ToS limits. Keep it
285	  personal-use and local; surface the caveat rather than hiding it.
286

Use when the user mentions ChordPro or .cho/.crd/.pro files, `[C]lyric` inline chords or `{title:}`/`{start_of_chorus}` directives, the `chordpro`/`a2crd` CLI, converting chords-over-lyrics (Ultimate Guitar/OnSong) text, making a guitar chord sheet for a song by name, or extracting chords from a YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud link or mp3/wav. References chordpro.org.
4	---
5	
6	# chordpro
7	
8	Produce and work with [ChordPro](https://www.chordpro.org/) chord sheets — the
9	plain-text format where chords live inline in the lyrics as `[C]like [G]this`.
10	This skill is a **router that degrades gracefully**: it picks the most reliable
11	workflow for whatever the user actually has (a `.cho` file, a chords-over-lyrics
12	paste, bare lyrics, an audio file, or just a song title) and every path ends by
13	**validating** the output. It is honest about the one hard part — extracting
14	chords from raw audio is an ~80%-accurate *draft*, never an oracle — and falls
15	back to interactive, fill-in-the-gaps assistance instead of pretending otherwise.
16	
17	## When to use
18	
19	- User names **ChordPro** / `.cho` / `.crd` / `.chopro` / `.pro`, inline
20	  `[C]lyric` chords, or `{title:}` / `{start_of_chorus}` / `{soc}` directives.
21	- Convert an existing sheet: **chords-over-lyrics** text (Ultimate Guitar, OnSong,
22	  a lyric with chord letters on the line above) → ChordPro.
23	- Render / transpose / validate a `.cho` with the **`chordpro`** or **`a2crd`** CLI.
24	- "Make a chord sheet for <song>" starting from **lyrics only**, or from a
25	  **YouTube / Bilibili / SoundCloud link** or an **mp3 / wav** file.
26	- Ask about **lyrics sources** (Mojim/魔鏡, KKBOX, Musixmatch, LRCLIB, Genius,
27	  NetEase, QQ Music) — which give time-synced `.lrc` vs plain text.
28	
29	## When NOT to use
30	
31	- **Engraving staff notation** (notes on a staff, MusicXML / MIDI / LilyPond /
32	  MuseScore output) — ChordPro is lyrics+chords, not a score. Hand off to a
33	  notation tool. (ChordPro *can* embed ABC/LilyPond fragments — see the format
34	  reference — but it is not an engraver.)
35	- **OMR from a scanned score image** (photo/PDF of printed sheet music → notes)
36	  is out of scope; there is no reliable open path. Offer manual transcription
37	  into ChordPro instead, and say so plainly.
38	
39	## Authoritative sources
40	
41	- Format + directives + CLI: **https://www.chordpro.org/** (link, don't
42	  paraphrase from memory — the directive set evolves).
43	- Source / releases: **https://github.com/ChordPro/chordpro**.
44	
45	## The router — pick the workflow by what the user has
46	
47	| User has… | Do this | Reliability |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| A `.cho`/`.crd`/`.pro` file | Render / transpose / **validate** via `chordpro` CLI | High |
50	| **Chords-over-lyrics** text (UG/OnSong) | `a2crd` → light manual cleanup → validate | High |
51	| A **known song** (title / lyrics / a link) and no chords yet | **Search existing chord charts online** → adapt to ChordPro (often via `a2crd`) → validate. See `references/chord-tab-sources.md` | Med–High (**best first move**) |
52	| **Lyrics only**, no chart found | Fetch/confirm lyrics → **interactively** fill chords (propose from key, ask the user to confirm/correct) | Medium (human-in-loop) |
53	| An **audio file or link**, want a machine draft | `scripts/audio-to-chords.py` → *draft* with `AUTO-GENERATED` header → human correction | ~80% (last resort) |
54	
55	Prefer the highest row that fits. Two rules that matter: don't jump to the audio
56	pipeline when the user already pasted chords (`a2crd` is faster and correct); and
57	for a **named/popular song, search for an existing human-made chart first** — it's
58	usually more accurate than audio ACR and sidesteps the download-ToS problem
59	entirely.
60	
61	## ChordPro cheat-sheet + output template
62	
63	- **Extensions**: `.cho` (recommended), also `.crd` `.chopro` `.chord` `.pro`.
64	  Plain UTF-8. `#` starts a comment line; blank lines separate blocks.
65	- **Inline chords**: `[C]` immediately before the syllable it sits over —
66	  `Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot`. Annotations (non-chords): `[*softly]`.
67	- **Metadata**: `{title:}`/`{t:}`, `{subtitle:}`/`{st:}`, `{artist:}`,
68	  `{composer:}`, `{album:}`, `{year:}`, `{key:}`, `{tempo:}`, `{time:}`, `{capo:}`.
69	- **Environments** (long / short): chorus `{start_of_chorus}`/`{soc}` …
70	  `{end_of_chorus}`/`{eoc}`; verse `{sov}`…`{eov}`; bridge `{sob}`…`{eob}`;
71	  tab (monospaced, chords NOT parsed) `{sot}`…`{eot}`. Recall a chorus with
72	  `{chorus}`. Comments: `{comment:}`/`{c:}`.
73	
74	Emit this shape — metadata block → environments/comments → verses/choruses:
75	
76	```
77	{title: Swing Low Sweet Chariot}
78	{artist: Traditional}
79	{key: G}
80	{tempo: 90}
81	{time: 4/4}
82	
83	{comment: Intro}
84	[G] [C] [G] [D]
85	
86	{start_of_chorus: Chorus}
87	Swing [G]low, sweet [C]chari[G]ot,
88	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
89	{end_of_chorus}
90	
91	{start_of_verse: Verse 1}
92	I [G]looked over Jordan, and [C]what did I [G]see,
93	Comin' for to carry me [D]home.
94	{end_of_verse}
95	
96	{chorus}
97	```
98	
99	Full directive set (chord `{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup, ABC/LilyPond
100	blocks, `x_` custom namespace) → read `references/chordpro-format.md`.
101	
102	## The `chordpro` / `a2crd` CLI (essentials)
103	
104	The official tool is a Perl program (CPAN dist **`App::Music::ChordPro`**). Current
105	6.x releases install the **`chordpro`** command; the chords-over-lyrics importer
106	is `chordpro --a2crd` (a standalone `a2crd` binary shipped in older releases and
107	may be absent — prefer `chordpro --a2crd`).
108	
109	```bash
110	# Install (macOS — there is NO official Homebrew formula; use CPAN)
111	brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro
112	# If `chordpro` then errors "Can't locate ChordPro.pm", activate local::lib once:
113	eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"   # add to ~/.zshrc to persist
114	
115	# Render
116	chordpro -o song.pdf song.cho          # PDF (format inferred from extension)
117	chordpro --generate=HTML -o song.html song.cho
118	
119	# Transpose (N semitones; suffix s/f forces sharp/flat spelling)
120	chordpro -x 2  -o up.pdf   song.cho
121	chordpro -x -3f -o down.pdf song.cho
122	
123	# Convert chords-over-lyrics text -> ChordPro (the official importer)
124	chordpro --a2crd input.txt -o song.cho
125	```
126	
127	Install-per-platform, generators, config JSON, songbook `--toc`, and `a2crd`
128	heuristic tuning → read `references/cli-and-rendering.md`.
129	
130	## Verify loop — never hand back an unvalidated `.cho`
131	
132	Every generated or edited file goes through the parser before you present it:
133	
134	```bash
135	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # wraps the command below; PASS/FAIL + warnings
136	# equivalently:
137	chordpro --strict --generate=Text -o - song.cho   # exit 0 + no stderr warnings = valid
138	```
139	
140	To auto-normalize to canonical form (fix spacing, round-trip directives):
141	`chordpro --generate=ChordPro -o song.cho song.cho`. If `chordpro` isn't
142	installed, the script prints the install one-liner — say so and offer to proceed
143	without rendering (the format is still human-checkable).
144	
145	## Finding existing chord charts (the usual first move)
146	
147	For a named/popular song, a human-made chart almost always already exists online
148	and beats audio extraction on accuracy. Search chart sites, pull the
149	**chords-over-lyrics** block, run it through `chordpro --a2crd`, then validate:
150	
151	```bash
152	# 1. search (中文: 吉他谱/和弦/弹唱谱; EN: chords / ultimate guitar)
153	# 2. WebFetch the best hit, copy the chords-over-lyrics into chart.txt
154	chordpro --a2crd chart.txt -o song.cho   # 3. convert
155	scripts/validate-cho.sh song.cho          # 4. validate
156	```
157	
158	Caption the result with a `{comment:}` naming the source and "published
159	arrangement — verify against the recording (capo/key may differ)". This is *not*
160	machine ACR, so don't use the `AUTO-GENERATED` header — but a web chart is still
161	one person's arrangement, not ground truth. Site catalog (91譜/Chord4/Ultimate
162	Guitar/…), format taxonomy, and legality → read `references/chord-tab-sources.md`.
163	
164	## Generating from audio / links — the fallback when no chart exists
165	
166	This is the shakiest path — reach for it only when no existing chart is available.
167	
168	**Set expectations first**: open automatic chord recognition tops out around **78–80% on simple major/minor pop**
169	and drops sharply on 7ths, extended/jazz chords, key changes, and quiet or dense
170	mixes; inversions/slash chords are unreliable; and it cannot know the capo a
171	guitarist used. Treat the result as a **draft to correct**, not a transcription.
172	
173	```bash
174	# Best-effort turnkey: link or local file -> draft ChordPro
175	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py --dry-run "https://youtu.be/..."   # show the plan first
176	uv run scripts/audio-to-chords.py -o draft.cho "https://youtu.be/..."
177	```
178	
179	The script downloads audio with `yt-dlp` (YouTube/Bilibili/SoundCloud) and runs
180	`chord-extractor`/Chordino. Its output **must** carry the
181	`{comment: AUTO-GENERATED — verify chords/key/timing}` header. On macOS the
182	Chordino Vamp plugin often isn't installed; the script detects that and prints
183	exact install guidance + manual alternatives instead of crashing — relay that to
184	the user rather than silently failing. Tool comparison, beat/key detection, and
185	commercial escape hatches (Moises/Songsterr have APIs; Chordify/Chord AI/Ultimate
186	Guitar don't) → read `references/audio-to-chords.md`.
187	
188	**Legal**: only process content the user owns or has the right to use, for
189	personal use, locally; downloading copyrighted audio can violate a platform's
190	ToS. Surface this — don't bury it.
191	
192	## Lyrics sources
193	
194	Default to **LRCLIB** — free, no API key, returns time-synced `.lrc`:
195	
196	```bash
197	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --artist "Adele" --track "Hello" --duration 295
198	uv run scripts/fetch-lyrics.py --plain --artist "..." --track "..."   # plain text
199	```
200	
201	| Source | Access | Synced `.lrc`? |
202	|---|---|---|
203	| **LRCLIB** | free, no key | **yes** |
204	| Musixmatch | API key; full/synced is paid | yes (paid) |
205	| NetEase / QQ Music | unofficial community APIs | yes (Chinese catalog) |
206	| Genius (`lyricsgenius`) | API token; lyrics scraped from page | no (plain) |
207	| Mojim / 魔鏡 | scrape-only | no (plain) |
208	| KKBOX | partner-gated | n/a |
209	
210	Full comparison, legality, and the LRCLIB API → read `references/lyrics-sources.md`.
211	
212	## Available scripts
213	
214	- **`scripts/validate-cho.sh <file.cho>`** — verify a file parses cleanly
215	  (`chordpro --strict`); PASS/FAIL to stdout, warnings to stderr. Guides install
216	  if `chordpro` is missing. Flags: `--help`.
217	- **`scripts/fetch-lyrics.py`** — fetch lyrics from LRCLIB (synced `.lrc` default,
218	  `--plain` for text). Self-contained via `uv run`. Flags: `--artist`, `--track`,
219	  `--duration`, `--album`, `--plain`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
220	- **`scripts/audio-to-chords.py`** — best-effort link/audio → draft ChordPro
221	  (`yt-dlp` + `chord-extractor`). Degrades gracefully when the ACR backend is
222	  unavailable. Flags: `-o/--output`, `--lrc`, `--help`, `--dry-run`.
223	
224	## Bundled assets
225	
226	Ready-to-open examples + a template under `assets/` (all songs are **public
227	domain**; every `.cho` validates clean with `chordpro --strict`). Use them as
228	copy-paste starting points and few-shot references:
229	
230	- `assets/example-amazing-grace.cho` — simplest real song: metadata + inline chords.
231	- `assets/example-when-the-saints.cho` — chorus/verse structure + `{chorus}` recall.
232	- `assets/example-greensleeves.cho` — feature showcase: `{define}` diagrams, a
233	  `{sot}` tab block, chorus recall, transpose note.
234	- `assets/template-song.cho` — fill-in-the-blanks scaffold (renders as-is); the
235	  starting point for the interactive chord-fill flow.
236	- `assets/example-synced-lyrics.lrc` — sample time-synced `.lrc` (what
237	  `fetch-lyrics.py` returns; feed it to `audio-to-chords.py --lrc`).
238	- `assets/example-a2crd-input.txt` — chords-over-lyrics plain text; convert with
239	  `chordpro --a2crd assets/example-a2crd-input.txt`.
240	
241	## Reference files
242	
243	- `references/chordpro-format.md` — Read **when** hand-authoring or you need a
244	  directive beyond the cheat-sheet (`{define}` diagrams, `{transpose}`, markup,
245	  ABC/LilyPond, `x_` custom namespace).
246	- `references/chord-tab-sources.md` — Read **when** you need chords for a named
247	  song and have none: where to find existing charts (91譜/Chord4/Ultimate
248	  Guitar/…), how to adapt them, and the legality.
249	- `references/cli-and-rendering.md` — Read **when** installing, rendering,
250	  transposing, converting with `a2crd`, or validating/normalizing.
251	- `references/audio-to-chords.md` — Read **when** the user wants chords from an
252	  audio file or a link (ACR tool choice, beat/key, limits, escape hatches).
253	- `references/lyrics-sources.md` — Read **when** fetching lyrics (source table,
254	  synced-vs-plain, API-vs-scrape, legality, LRCLIB API).
255	
256	## Gotchas
257	
258	- **macOS has no official Homebrew `chordpro`** — install via CPAN
259	  (`brew install perl cpanminus && cpanm App::Music::ChordPro`). A signed `.dmg`
260	  GUI exists on GitHub Releases but the CLI is the CPAN route.
261	- **`Can't locate ChordPro.pm in @INC` after cpanm** — cpanm installed into a
262	  `local::lib` (`~/perl5`) that isn't on Perl's path. Activate it:
263	  `eval "$(perl -I"$HOME/perl5/lib/perl5" -Mlocal::lib)"` (persist in `~/.zshrc`).
264	- **No standalone `a2crd` in ChordPro 6.x** — use `chordpro --a2crd input.txt`.
265	  Its output needs a human pass (heuristic, column-based chord placement); always
266	  validate and eyeball before rendering.
267	- **Angle brackets `< >` are text markup in ChordPro v6.** Don't put `<...>`
268	  placeholders in lyrics/chords — the parser reads `<b>`/`<i>`-style markup and
269	  floods warnings. Use plain-text placeholders (see `assets/template-song.cho`).
270	- **No official online validator.** chordpro.org hosts docs + a desktop GUI, not
271	  a "try it online" box. Validate locally with the CLI (`validate-cho.sh`).
272	- **Chord accuracy from audio is ~80% at best** on simple pop, worse otherwise.
273	  Never present a machine-extracted sheet without the `AUTO-GENERATED` header and
274	  a "verify chords/key/timing" caveat.
275	- **Auto-generated chart sites are ACR in disguise.** Chordu / Chordify /
276	  GuitarTuna charts are machine-derived (~80%, same caveat) — treat them as drafts,
277	  unlike human-made charts on 91譜 / Chord4 / Ultimate Guitar.
278	- **Detected key is a suggestion.** ACR outputs absolute pitches; key detection
279	  confuses relative major/minor and keys a fifth apart, and enharmonic spelling
280	  (Gb vs F#) is ambiguous. Confirm with the user before committing `{key:}`.
281	- **Chords in `{sot}`…`{eot}` tab blocks are NOT parsed** — that's for ASCII tab.
282	  Use inline `[..]` in verses/choruses; reserve tab blocks for fret diagrams.
283	- **Lyrics/audio ToS.** Prefer LRCLIB (open); most other lyric sources are
284	  scrape-only or paid, and downloading audio has copyright/ToS limits. Keep it
285	  personal-use and local; surface the caveat rather than hiding it.
286
